title.narrative: Transboundary Water Support through the Global Facility for Transboundary Water Cooperation

description.narrative: Foster cooperative management of shared freshwater ecosystems and promote the global transboundary water (TBW) agenda for improved water security and resilience to climate change in shared basins.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

This Project will benefit riparian governments as well as river basin and transboundary aquifer organizations in various ways. Just-in-time support delivered under Pillar 1 is designed to prepare investments that will contribute to the achievement of global environmental benefits as well as transboundary water cooperation. Furthermore, training and development of tools under Pillar 2 will enhance institutional capacity of riparian governments and river basin and aquifer organizations on issues such as flood forecasting, decision support, water accounting, aimed at enhancing climate resilience and sustainable management of shared resources. Knowledge exchange and outreach supported under Pillar 3 are intended to foster new partnerships that facilitate achievement of GEBs and adaptation benefits (e.g. through new partnerships between riparian governments or organizations with development partners).-----------------Stakeholder consultation - brief summary and list of names and dates of consultationsThe 2nd Global Forum on Transboundary Waters held on June 19-20, 2025, in Geneva, co-hosted by the World Bank, Switzerland and the UNECE Secretariat of the Water Convention, provided opportunity to engage with around 90 delegates representing river basin organizations, governments and financing partners from all over the world. The Forum resulted among other in a request for support on innovative financing from the Senegal River Basin Commission (OMVS) as well as support from bilateral partners to collaborate on their initiative related to the Gambia Basin on the same topic. During the 3rd Pan-African Implementation and Partnership Conference on Water (PANAFCON-3) held May 27-29, 2025 in Lusaka, the stakeholder engagement for the Pan-African Study was launched during a session including high-level speakers such as Dr Rashid Mbaziira, Executive Secretary of AMCOW, Harsen Nyambe, Blue Economy and Sustainable Environment Director of the African Union, and Dr Florence Adongo, President of the African Network of Basin Organisations (ANBO) as well as representation of EU and Germany/GIZ in the panel.
